neon.tip: Cardinal: the red stripe runs the whole length of the belly, from the gills to the tail. Neon: the red covers only the rear half of the body. Green neon: much smaller, with a short red patch near the tail.

rummy.tip: True rummy-nose (Hemigrammus): red on the nose only, with clean black-and-white tail bars. Brilliant/false rummy (Petitella): the red covers more of the head and the tail bars are bolder.

bigtetra.tip: Congo: big scales with a rainbow sheen, males have flowing fins. Emperor: dark stripe along the body, with a longer extended tail middle. Buenos Aires and black skirt tetras are deeper-bodied with dark bands.

skirt.tip: Black skirt: wide black fade at the rear and tall fins. Serpae: red-orange body with a black shoulder spot. Bleeding heart: a single red spot behind the gill on a pink body.

redbarb.tip: Rosy: copper-pink body with a black tail base spot in males that glow rosy red. Cherry: red body with a dark stripe through the eye. Tiger: four black vertical bars with orange-red fins. Odessa: red stripe along the middle of the body. Gold and checkerboard: golden or spotted.

algae.tip: Siamese algae eater: a clean black stripe from the nose through the eye all the way to the end of the tail. Flying fox: a gold stripe above the black one, and the stripe stops at the tail base. Chinese algae eater: golden, larger sucker mouth and a blotchy stripe, grows big and aggressive.

cory.tip: Skunk: black stripe along the back with an orange tint. Panda: black eye patches, black tail base and dorsal spot. Bronze/Aeneus: plain metallic bronze or green. Albino: pale pink with red eyes. Julii: spotted head with lines. False julii: more lines. Peppered: dark pepper spots over gray. Sterbai: dark with orange pectoral fins. Pygmy: under 1 inch, swims mid-water.

loach.tip: Kuhli: thin eel-like with dark and tan bands. Clown: orange with black bands and red fins. Yoyo: marks that read "Y-O-Y-O" along the body. Zebra: pale with dark vertical stripes. Dojo/weather loach: long, plain, whiskered. Hillstream: flat, clings to glass.

rainbow.tip: Boesemani: front half blue-gray, back half orange-yellow. Turquoise: blue-green overall. Australian/splendid: stripe along the side with orange fins. Dwarf neon: under 2 inches with a red-stripe fade. Red: all red males. Threadfin: very tall twin dorsal fins.

guppy.tip: Endler: under an inch and a half, bright pattern, small tail. Guppy: larger, big fan-like tail in many colors. Platy: stockier with a rounded tail. Swordtail: males have a long sword on the tail. Molly: larger and taller with a big dorsal fin.

danio.tip: Zebra: horizontal blue-white stripes. Pearl: pearly sheen with a pink stripe. Leopard: spots instead of stripes. White cloud: tiny with a red tail base and a gold stripe. Celestial pearl danio: tiny with pale spots on dark blue.

rasbora.tip: Harlequin: copper body with a black triangle. Lambchop: thinner, longer black wedge. Espei: red-orange with a black wedge that starts at the middle. Chili: tiny and bright red. Scissortail: black-and-white striped tail.

gourami.tip: Dwarf: small, with blue and red stripes. Honey: yellow-orange, small. Pearl: pearly spots with a dark line from nose to tail. Three-spot/blue/gold: larger, with a spot mid-body and one at the tail base. Kissing: pink, with big lips.

pleco.tip: Bristlenose: fleshy tentacles on the snout. Common: very large with a sail-like dorsal fin. Clown pleco: small with orange bands. Zebra pleco: small, bold black-and-white stripes. Otocinclus: tiny with a dark stripe, a flat sucker.

stick.tip: Twig catfish (Farlowella): very thin like a twig, with a long pointed snout. Whiptail (Rineloricaria): flatter body with a long thin whip-like tail.

cichmal.tip: Yellow lab: bright yellow with a black dorsal edge. Red zebra: orange to peach with a blotchy pattern. Cobalt zebra: blue with dark bars. Demasoni: small, blue with thick black bars. Kenyi: males yellow-orange, females blue bars. Peacocks: brilliant solid colors, long pointed body.

cichsa.tip: Angelfish: tall with long trailing fins. Oscar: large, with an orange-patterned dark body and a tail spot. Convict: black and white vertical stripes. Jack Dempsey: dark with bright blue-green flecks. Severum: round, with a faint orange or gold tint. Blue acara: gray-blue with a vertical dark bar behind the gill and blue speckles. Firemouth: red throat and belly. Keyhole: tiny with a keyhole-shaped spot.

dwarfcich.tip: German blue ram: blue-yellow with a black spot behind the head and red fins. Bolivian ram: duller, with a stripe over the eye. Apistogramma: small with a rounded tail, males show a dark horizontal stripe and a frilled dorsal.

tanganyika.tip: Julidochromis: elongated with black stripes. Princess (brichardi): elegant, with extended fins and a light blue edge. Shell dwellers: tiny, rest in shells. Cyprichromis: slender, free-swimming and in schools.

puffer.tip: Pea puffer: tiny yellow-green with brown spots. Figure-8: rounder, with a figure-8 pattern on its back. Both are small, rounded and slow-moving.

betta.tip: Betta males have long flowing fins; females and plakats have short fins. Paradise fish: striped with red and blue and a forked tail.

goldfish.tip: Common/comet: long body with a single tail. Fantail and Ryukin: rounded body with a double tail. Oranda: has a head hood. Koi: barbels and a wide range of colors.

shrimpf.tip: Cherry: bright red (Neocaridina). Crystal red: red and white bands. Amano: gray-clear with dotted lateral spots. Ghost/glass: fully transparent. Bamboo/wood: large and brown, with fan arms. Blue velvet: solid blue.

nerite.tip: Zebra nerite: black stripes on gold. Tiger nerite: bold dark stripes. Horned nerite: has little horns. Olive nerite: plain, with a speckled olive shell. Mystery/apple snail: large, round, smooth shell in gold, blue or ivory.

cfish.tip: Ocellaris: orange with three white bands and thin black edging. Percula: thicker black edging between bands and more rounded. Maroon: dark red with a single bright stripe. Clarkii: darker body with a yellow tail. Tomato: bright red-orange, with a single patch behind the eye.

tang.tip: Yellow: all bright yellow. Regal/blue/hippo: blue with a black palette shape and yellow tail. Purple: purple with a yellow tail. Kole: dark with a gold ring around the eye. Sailfin: tall with a large dorsal sail. Powder blue: sky blue with a white face and yellow dorsal.

damsel.tip: Blue-green chromis: bright blue-green, shoals in groups. Yellowtail damsel: royal blue with a yellow tail. Domino: black with white spots. Three-stripe: white with three black bars. Azure: blue and yellow.

gobyb.tip: Firefish: white nose and a red tail with a long dorsal spike. Yellow watchman: yellow body with a long dorsal fin. Lawnmower blenny: brown with a sloped face. Tailspot blenny: spotted with a stripe on the tail. Bicolor blenny: two-tone, with a dark head and yellow tail.

mandarin.tip: Mandarin: orange, blue and green swirls, slow along the rock. Psychedelic mandarin: the same but with a more intense maze-like pattern.

wrasse.tip: Six-line wrasse: six stripes. Melanurus: a black tail spot. Fairy wrasse: bright with long fins. Cleaner wrasse: thin blue stripe.

angel.tip: Flame angel: red-orange with vertical dark bars. Coral beauty: blue to orange with a dark shoulder. Copperband butterfly: long snout with a copper-colored stripe.

euph.tip: Hammer: heads with hammer-shaped or anchor tentacle tips. Frogspawn: branching tentacle tips like frog eggs. Torch: long single-tipped tentacles. Duncan: short, round, fleshy polyps on a small stony skeleton.

softc.tip: Xenia: pulsing, waving stalks. Green star polyps: bright green mats with small arms. Kenya tree: a tree-like stalk branching into small heads. Leather (toadstool): wide, thick cap that folds in. Clove polyps: dense stalks with pale tips.

zoa.tip: Zoanthid/palythoa: groups of small round polyps in colonies and mats. Mushrooms (Discosoma): flat disc, no stalk. Ricordea: flatter bumpy disks. Rhodactis: larger and hairy-looking.

sps.tip: Acropora: branching with a tip polyp. Montipora: plating or encrusting with tiny polyps. Birdsnest/Seriatopora: thin fine branches. Stylophora: thick branches.

lps.tip: Brain (Lobophyllia/Favia): round or dome-shaped with ridged, maze-like valleys. Trachyphyllia: flat and folded. Goniopora: long flowerpot-like polyps, delicate. Bubble coral: bubbly sacs. Candy cane: each polyp on its own stalk.

anemone.tip: Bubble-tip: bulb tips on tentacles. Long tentacle: long flowing tentacles and a bigger body. Carpet: flat, wide, sticky tentacles. Condy: long, thin tentacles with pink tips. Aiptasia: tiny glassy pest.

crab.tip: Blue-leg hermit: blue legs with orange bands. Red-leg hermit: red legs. Emerald crab: green, mostly stationary. Sally Lightfoot: bright red and orange, runs fast.

reefsnail.tip: Turbo: large and round, with a rough shell. Nassarius: small cones that burrow. Astraea: flat coin-like shell. Cerith: thin spiral.

sword.tip: Amazon sword (Echinodorus): large, wide leaves growing from a crown. Narrow-leaf swords: thinner leaves. Often large and stand in the middle or back of the tank.

crypt.tip: Crypts form a rosette with crinkled leaves. Wendtii: wavy leaves in green to bronze. Parva: tiny and compact. Balansae: long, strap-like leaves.

val.tip: Vallisneria: long, thin ribbon leaves. Sagittaria: grass-like blades on a base, usually shorter. Jungle val: giant and broad.

stem.tip: Ludwigia: oval leaves in pairs on a stem, red underside. Rotala: tiny narrow leaves in whorls, pink to red tips. Bacopa: thick round leaves. Hygrophila: pointy, often broad leaves. Alternanthera: red or maroon leaves.

fern.tip: Java fern: finger-like fronds, small black spots under leaves. Anubias: thick dark arrowhead leaves. Mosses: green fuzzy mats on wood or rocks. Bolbitis: wavy dark fronds.

float.tip: Frogbit: small round leaves with roots hanging down. Water lettuce: rosettes like tiny cabbages. Salvinia: round, hairy leaves. Duckweed: tiny dots covering the surface.

carpet.tip: Dwarf hairgrass: very fine grass-like carpet. Monte Carlo: rounded tiny leaves. Dwarf baby tears: tiny round leaves in a dense mat. Glosso: tiny paddle leaves.

macro.tip: Chaeto: fuzzy green balls or strands. Caulerpa: grape-like or feathery green runners. Halimeda: segmented, stiff.

c.n: Easy, colorful LPS that likes to be fed. Low to medium light, low to medium flow.
Branching SPS that needs very stable, clean water and strong light and flow. For experienced keepers.
A pest anemone that spreads fast and stings corals. Peppermint shrimp and copperband butterflies eat it.
Pale pink version of the bronze cory. Hardy, social and best kept in groups.
Maroon-red stem plant that needs strong light and iron. Looks great in a planted tank.
Larger, excellent algae eaters. Tough and clean-minded, though larvae need brackish water to grow.
Floating plant with long, trailing roots. Shades the tank and soaks up nutrients; useful for shy fish.
Big, hardy background plant with broad leaves. Heavy root feeder, so use root tabs.
Fast, easy stem plant that soaks up nutrients. Float it or plant it.
Tall, elegant cichlid that needs a tall tank. Adults may eat very small fish like neons; pairs defend breeding spots.
Colorful schooling fish that need feeding several times a day. Best for experienced keepers with larger tanks.
Tough, slow plant with dark leaves. Tie to wood or rock and do not bury the rhizome.
Small, colorful dwarf cichlid. Needs caves and plants; males hold territory.
Bulb plant with wavy leaves that likes a dormant spell. Good midground cover.
General plant entry. Look for the exact species name to see detailed care.
Shoots water at prey. Needs brackish water and a lid, and will eat small fish.
Hunts other snails. Use it to control pest snails, but not with snails you want to keep.
Active, silvery fish with orange fins. Needs a long tank, neutral to hard water and a group.
Bright blue and yellow damsel that gets territorial. Best with tough fish.
Hardy, thick stem plant with round leaves. Easy, good for beginners.
Filter feeder that fans food from the current. Needs good flow and a mature tank.
Small lily with banana-shaped roots. Easy; do not bury the roots.
Peaceful and calm, bred in captivity. Does best in pairs.
Males flare at their own reflection and fight other males. Likes warm, calm water with plants and slow tank mates.
Bold, two-toned blenny that lives in rock holes. May harass small, peaceful fish.
Fine-branched SPS that is easier than acropora. Medium to strong light and flow.
Hardy little school fish from Paraguay with a bold black and silver stripe. Do best in groups of six or more with plants.
A dark morph of the percula. Hardy, easy and a great beginner reef fish.
Peaceful, hardy tetra from the Amazon. Keep six or more.
Hardy and active, with a habit of nipping slow, long-finned fish. Keep six or more with similarly quick tank mates.
Easy, colorful LPS that likes low light. Hardy and good for beginners.
Tall pink tetra with a red spot behind the gill. Peaceful in a group but can nip fins when kept in small numbers.
Hardy, silver tetra that may nip long fins. Likes cooler temperatures and a group.
Hardy cichlid with a blue-gray body and dark bar behind the gill. Needs a roomy tank and can bother small fish.
Large and bold, will eat fish it catches and uproot plants. Best alone or with fast fish.
Sensitive starfish that needs a mature tank and slow acclimation. Often dies in new tanks.
Peaceful blue-tinted tetra from the Amazon. Keep in groups of six or more.
Deep blue cousin of the cherry shrimp. Hardy, breeds easily in planted tanks without fish that eat shrimp.
Peaceful schooling fish that is easy to keep. Good in groups of five or more.
Algae cleaner that will take new snail shells. Needs spare shells.
Digs burrows, so needs deep sand and rubble. Peaceful and a jumper.
Blue in front and orange behind, calm and colorful. Likes neutral to hard water, a long tank and a group of six or more.
Dark, wavy fronds that grow on wood or stone. Slow starter but beautiful once settled.
Hardier than the German blue ram, peaceful and calm. Likes sand, plants and caves.
Easy, fleshy LPS that likes low to medium light. Can sting neighbors at night.
The bolder-patterned cousin of the rummy-nose, schooling in open water. Keep warm, clean and in a group of eight or more.
Small, hardy pleco that eats algae and wood. Needs driftwood to chew and plenty of hiding spots.
Hardy scavenger that hides by day. Some species may grab small fish.
Hardy and common cory. Needs a group of six or more and smooth sand or gravel.
Bubble-like sacs by day and sweeper tentacles at night. Needs space and medium light, low flow.
Common host for clownfish. Needs strong light and a mature tank, and may wander and sting corals.
Slow, shimmery plant that grows on wood and rock. Hardy and good for nano tanks.
Hardy, active and plant-nibbling, best in a roomy tank. May bother small, slow tank mates.
Black-and-yellow Malawi mbuna. Aggressive and territorial; needs hard water and rocks.
Tiny brackish goby with bold stripes. Needs a little salt, caves and quiet tank mates.
Feathery stem that needs good light and nutrients. Beautiful but often melts in poor conditions.
Easy, hardy LPS that grows in clumps. Low to medium light, gentle flow.
Slightly larger and warmer-loving than the neon, from blackwater Amazon streams. Needs a school of eight or more, soft water and plants for cover.
Huge and potent stinger that eats fish. Needs a large tank and experienced keeper.
Fast-growing macroalgae that can spread. Can go sexual and cloud the water, so keep it contained.
Tiny and shy, with a pearly spotted pattern. Prefers a calm planted tank and similarly gentle tank mates.
Small, tough sand and rock cleaner. Good at eating diatoms and detritus.
Tangled, ball-like macroalgae that soaks up nutrients. Great in a refugium.
Colorful, spreading coral that likes low to medium light. Can sting neighbors.
One of the gentlest barbs, red males show off in planted tanks. Keep six or more with calm tank mates.
Hardy, bright red shrimp that breed easily. Need moss, plants and no small-mouthed predators.
Small dwarf angel that may nip corals. Needs a mature tank.
Tiny and bright red; needs a calm nano tank and tiny, gentle tank mates. Keep a large group.
Sold as an algae eater but gets large and aggressive. Often bullies other bottom fish.
Colorful filter feeder that burrows into live rock or coral. Needs good flow.
Tough, adaptable clownfish that hosts many anemones. Can be bossy with other clownfish.
Cleans fish and eats scraps. Needs stable salinity and no copper.
Difficult; most starve in captivity. Not recommended for most aquariums.
Hardy, easy polyps that wave their tentacles. Medium light and flow.
Playful, social, long-lived loach that grows large. Needs a big tank, a group and plenty of hiding places.
Tiny, wood-eating pleco with orange bands. Needs real driftwood and caves.
Huge and aggressive. Eats corals and inverts, so only in fish-only tanks.
Striking blue mbuna from Lake Malawi. Needs hard, alkaline water and plenty of rockwork.
Grows huge and makes lots of waste, despite its cute juvenile size. Needs a very large tank.
Sand-sifting snail that eats algae and leftovers. Needs a mature tank.
Hardy, longer-tentacled anemone that hosts few clownfish. May sting nearby corals and sometimes wanders.
Big-scaled, rainbow-sheened schooler from Africa. Calm, but needs a roomy tank, soft water and plenty of plants.
Hardy, aggressive cichlid that breeds readily and guards its territory. Better with tough tank mates.
Eats Aiptasia but is hard to feed and delicate. Not for beginners.
Hardy dwarf angel that may nip some corals. Needs a mature, large tank.
Pink and purple crust that spreads over rock. A sign of a stable tank.
Peaceful, social bottom feeders. Need sand or smooth gravel and a group of six or more.
Large bulb plant with long leaves. Tough but needs room and root tabs.
Tiny, bright clam that bores into rock. Needs very strong light and stable parameters.
Rosette plants that melt when moved, then grow back. Do best with root tabs and stable conditions.
Delicate red-and-white shrimp that need soft, stable water and no fish that eat shrimp.
Grassy, feathery plant that makes a bushy background. Easy and good for beginners.
Open-water Tanganyikan schooler. Needs a long tank, hard alkaline water and no bullies.
Tiny but very aggressive mbuna from Lake Malawi. Needs a crowded group to share aggression.
Big, active schooling barb with a red-and-black stripe. Needs a long tank with strong flow and room to swim.
Large, bright clam needing strong light and stable parameters. Needs plenty of space.
Peaceful schooler with sparkly scales and flowing fins on the males. Needs a roomy tank and a group of six or more.
Stately, sensitive cichlid that needs warm, soft, very clean water. Keep in groups with calm tank mates.
Eats corals and inverts, and gets large. Needs a big fish-only tank.
Hardy, cool-water loach that wriggles and buries. Needs a lid and smooth sand.
Hardy but bossy, with white spots on black. Best added last to a tank.
Brilliant but bossy. Often picks on peaceful tank mates, so add it last.
Tiny floating plant that soaks up nutrients. Spreads fast and is hard to remove.
Easy LPS with pale tentacles that lets you grow it from small heads. Low to medium light, gentle flow.
Famous but fussy carpet plant. Needs strong light, CO2 and good nutrients.
Tiny crayfish that can still grab slow fish and shrimp. Needs hiding spots and calm tank mates.
Colorful but prone to disease; best bought from a trusted source. Gets along with calm fish and plenty of plants.
Fine lawn plant that needs strong light and CO2 to carpet.
Small, peaceful rainbowfish that suits smaller planted tanks. Keep six or more.
Tiny, peaceful and sensitive. Keep in a calm, planted tank with small tank mates.
Grassy foreground that spreads by runners. Easy and hardy.
Metallic blue Malawi hap, calmer than mbuna. Likes hard, alkaline water and open swimming room.
Delicate, long-tentacle coral prone to infections. Needs a very stable tank.
Electric, trunk-nosed fish that needs sand, caves and slow, calm tank mates.
One of the smallest tetras, glowing orange in a planted nano tank. Keep a big group and avoid pushy tank mates.
Metallic-green armored catfish, related to corys. Needs a group and sand.
Eats bubble algae and hair algae. Usually reef-safe; can nibble corals when hungry.
Dark, elegant schooling fish from Colombia. Peaceful and suited to a planted tank with a group of six or more.
Tiny, vivid livebearers that breed quickly. Best in a calm tank; small size makes them a snack for bigger fish.
Builds large tunnels and moves sand. Needs deep sand and a lid.
Colorful and active. Needs a lid and a calm tank.
Small, perching hawkfish that snaps up shrimp. Hardy and entertaining.
Filter-feeding worm that fans out from a tube. Needs good flow and some live food.
Needs brackish water to thrive and eats snails. Aggressive; best kept alone.
Bright red, shy shrimp that likes caves. Needs stable salinity and no copper.
Peaceful, shy and a jumper. Needs a lid and a calm tank.
Red-throated cichlid that flares dramatically. Keep with robust tank mates.
Beautiful dwarf angel that may nip some corals. Needs a mature, large tank.
Perches on rocks and snaps up shrimp and small fish. Hardy and fun to watch.
Algae-eating fish that can get territorial with its own kind. Needs current, wood and rock cover.
Algae grazer with venomous spines. Needs a large tank and careful handling.
Branching coral with long stinging tentacles. Medium light, gentle flow; needs space.
Big Lake Tanganyika cichlid with a prominent forehead. Needs a large tank and hard, alkaline water.
Shy, jewel-colored dwarf cichlid that needs warm, soft, very clean water. Not for new tanks.
Large nocturnal fish that hunts smaller tank mates. Needs a very large, calm tank.
Clear, cheap shrimp that clean up leftovers. Easily eaten by most fish.
Low carpet with paddle leaves. Needs very strong light and CO2.
Peaceful small tetra with a glowing orange stripe. Good in groups of six or more in a planted tank.
Hardy, golden barb that likes cooler temperatures. May nip fins when kept in small numbers.
Hardy, golden tetra that stays calm. Keep six or more.
Messy, cool-water fish that need far more space than they are sold with. Not a match for tropical tanks.
Delicate flower pot coral that needs stable conditions and regular feeding. Not for beginners.
Fan or branching coral that needs good flow. Photosynthetic types do best.
Tiny and shy, from slow Amazon streams. Keep in a calm planted tank with similarly small, gentle tank mates.
Needs brackish water as an adult and eats snails. Aggressive; best alone.
Fast, easy mat-forming coral. Can take over rocks, so give it its own island.
Large, aggressive cichlid with a vivid blue-green pattern. Needs a big tank and sturdy tank mates.
Bright, easy livebearers that breed quickly. Long-finned males are nipped by barbs and other fin-nippers.
Segmented, calcifying macroalgae. Needs calcium and decent light.
Easy, with long sweeping tentacles that sting neighbors. Medium light, gentle flow; needs space.
Easy, peaceful schooling fish with a black triangle. Keep eight or more with plants.
Eats only starfish. Needs a supply of live sea stars and an experienced keeper.
Big, striking wrasse that eats shrimp and crabs. Needs a large, fish-only tank.
Surface-living fish that glide above the water. Keep a tight lid, floating plants and calm tank mates.
Flat, suction-cup loach from fast, cool streams. Needs cool, well-oxygenated water and strong current.
The gentlest gourami. Shy, calm and good for peaceful planted tanks.
Armored catfish that makes noises and eats leftovers. Peaceful but can eat very small fish at night.
Algae eater with tiny horns. Needs hard water for its shell.
Floating or planted, fast-growing stem. Great at soaking up nutrients; sheds needles.
Easy, fast stem plant with broad leaves. Needs regular trimming.
Bold, aggressive cichlid with bright blue speckles. Needs a large tank and tough tank mates.
Hardy, slow plant that you tie to wood or rock. Do not bury the rhizome.
Easy, fuzzy moss that holds baby fish and shrimp. Great on wood and rock.
Small Tanganyikan cichlid that lives among rocks. Needs hard, alkaline water; pairs defend territory.
Spotted and striped cory, peaceful and social. Keep a group on soft sand.
Fast-growing soft coral that makes a tree-like colony. Easy and frag-friendly.
Males turn yellow and bully others. Needs hard, alkaline water and plenty of rock.
Small, calm cichlid with a dark keyhole spot. Good for community tanks with gentle tank mates.
Colorful, short-lived fish, often kept in species tanks. Needs a lid and calm, slow tank mates.
Pink, large and boisterous. Kisses are really wrestling; needs a big tank and tough tank mates.
Pond fish that grow very large. Not suited to home aquariums.
Hardy algae grazer with a golden eye ring. A great clean-up fish for reefs.
Shy, eel-like loach that hides by day. Needs a group, sand and cover.
Bright, hardy African cichlid from Lake Victoria. Needs hard water and tough tank mates.
A peaceful, slimmer relative of the harlequin. Keep eight or more in a planted tank.
Algae grazer with a lot of personality. Gets territorial with other blennies.
Hardy, large soft coral that releases chemicals that can stress neighbors. Run carbon.
Peaceful and hardy Amazon schooler that glows yellow-gold in planted tanks. Keep six or more.
Bright yellow dwarf angel that may nip corals. Needs a mature tank.
Spotted cousin of the zebra danio. Very active; keep a group and a tight lid.
Grass-like foreground plant that spreads by runners. Likes good light.
Venomous predator that eats fish and shrimp. Needs a large tank and no small tank mates.
Hosts clownfish. Needs strong light and a stable tank, and may sting neighboring corals.
Elegant, perching hawkfish that will eat shrimp and tiny fish. Needs rocks to sit on.
Easy stem plant with red leaves under bright light. Good beginner colorful plant.
Burrowing snail that turns sand and eats waste. Breeds easily.
Colorful and delicate. Needs a mature tank full of live pods and calm tank mates.
Grows from propagules in brackish or salt water. Slow and soaks up nutrients, great in a sump.
Round green algae balls that need the occasional roll. Very easy.
Bold, large clownfish that gets aggressive with age. Best kept as a bonded pair in a bigger tank.
Giant clam needing very strong light and stable calcium. Not for beginners.
Active and hardy, eats pests such as flatworms. Needs a lid and can bully timid fish.
Oak-shaped leaves on a sturdy stem. Easy and good for beginners.
Hardy livebearer that likes hard, alkaline water and sometimes a little salt. Best in groups with more females.
Silver, flat brackish fish that lives in schools. Needs salt as it matures.
Carpeting plant with tiny leaves. Needs strong light and CO2.
Plating or encrusting SPS that is easier than acropora. Needs strong light and good flow.
Amphibious brackish fish. Needs land to climb onto and a lid.
Very hardy, low-light coral. Spreads and floats across rocks.
Large, colorful snail that eats algae and leftovers. Breeds if both sexes are kept.
Burrowing scavenger that keeps sand clean. Needs sand to bury in.
Tiny cleaner goby that works over rocks. Peaceful and good for nano reefs.
Peaceful South American schooler from slow, shaded streams. Keep six or more in a planted tank with dim spots and floating plants.
Hardy and the classic reef fish. Pairs bond for life and may host anemones or other soft hosts.
Red-striped, active barb that likes cooler water. Keep in groups of six or more.
Quiet algae eater with an olive shell. Needs hard water for a healthy shell.
Big, smart and messy. Eats any fish that fits in its mouth; needs a huge tank and a strong filter.
Tiny algae eater. Needs a mature tank with biofilm and algae, plus a group.
Spotted, peaceful and nocturnal. Good in pairs or small groups.
Easy, matted coral that grows quickly. Contains palytoxin, so handle with gloves.
Small, black-eyed cory that likes slightly cooler water. Needs sand and a group of six or more.
Tough, aggressive cousin of the betta. Needs room and robust tank mates; males fight.
Tiny but a fierce nipper that eats snails and shrimp. Best in a species tank or with very hardy fish.
Brilliant Malawi cichlid with sandy habitat needs. Needs hard, alkaline water and peaceful-ish tank mates.
Active, pearly schooler that likes cooler water. Keep a group and a tight lid.
Peaceful, pearl-spotted gourami with long fins. Males can spar; likes floating plants.
Slim, peaceful fish that likes dim light and soft water. Keep six or more with calm tank mates.
Peaceful schooler with a black stripe, easy to keep. Best in a group of six or more with plants.
Easy plant with round leaves that grows quickly on the surface or planted. Good for beginners.
Cool-water cory, hardy and social. Prefers a group and soft sand.
Eats Aiptasia anemones, though some also pick at corals.
Very close to the ocellaris, with thicker black edges. Hardy, bonded pairs and good reef fish.
Aggressive and destructive. Eats corals and inverts, so only in fish-only tanks.
Silver, spotted catfish with long whiskers, active at night. Will eat small fish like neons.
Delicate and slow, needs live food and gentle tank mates. Not for beginners.
Digs burrows and often pairs with a goby. Noisy snapping claw.
Free-living, flat coral that rests on sand. Medium light, gentle flow.
Hardy, peaceful livebearers in many colors. Do well in groups and breed easily.
Feathery, lush stem plant like star grass. Likes strong light and CO2.
Hardy, fast-breeding snail. Often arrives on plants and eats algae and waste.
Eats corals and inverts, and gets large. Needs a big fish-only tank.
Beautiful but delicate and prone to ich. Needs a large tank and an experienced keeper.
Elegant Tanganyikan cichlid with long fins. Keep in a group with hard alkaline water.
Needs a mature reef rich in live pods. Not for new tanks.
Beautiful but aggressive with other tangs. Needs a large tank and good algae.
The smallest cory, often swimming mid-water. Needs a big group and calm, small tank mates.
Large, slow snail that eats algae and waste. Needs warm, stable water and hard water for its shell.
Aggressive toward other bottom dwellers and its own kind. Best kept alone or with similarly large fish.
Hardy, breeds readily and cleans up leftovers. Some people find them a pest.
Red macroalgae that soaks up nutrients and feeds tangs. Easy to grow.
Peaceful, with glowing red males in a group. Prefers harder water and plenty of swimming room.
Turns red under strong light. Likes nutrient-rich water and clear space at the surface.
Bold lily with red leaves. Pinches off pads that reach the surface.
Active mbuna from Lake Malawi. Needs hard alkaline water, rocks and a crowded-looking tank to spread aggression.
Hardy and common, but will take snail shells and may bother snails.
Territorial, aggressive and best kept alone. Needs hiding spots and a large tank.
Needs a large tank and a lot of swimming room. Prone to ich in new setups.
Hairy, large mushroom that tolerates a range of light. Hardy and fast growing.
Colorful, bumpy mushroom that likes low to medium light. Easy once settled.
Hardy and active, males glow rosy red. Cooler water than most tropical fish; may nip slower fish with long fins.
Peaceful, silvery fish with a rosy flush on the fins. Best in a school of six or more.
Fine stem plant that turns pink to red under strong light. Better with CO2.
Purple and yellow, hardy and peaceful with non-grammas. Needs caves and rocks to hide in.
Calm algae eater with a sucker mouth. Needs wood and caves.
Tight-schooling fish from the Amazon and a good water-quality canary. Likes soft, clean, warm water and a big group.
Large and active, with a tall sail-like dorsal fin. Needs a big tank and lots of algae.
Fast, bold crab that eats algae and may snatch small fish or inverts.
Small, hairy floating plant. Easy and good for shading.
Brackish schooling fish that eats plants. Needs salt and a big tank as it matures.
Larger, quick schooling fish with a black-and-white scissor tail. Needs a long tank and a lid.
Large single-polyp coral with vivid colors. Low light, gentle flow.
Can release toxins if stressed. Needs a mature tank with sand.
Slow, delicate feeders needing calm, cool water and plenty of live food. Not with fast fish.
Ancient-looking predator that hunts at night. Needs a large tank, a tight lid and no small tank mates.
Lively red tetra that nips long fins if kept in small groups. Keep a school of eight or more and avoid long-finned tank mates.
Large, calm-for-a-cichlid fish with a round body. Needs a roomy tank and good filtration.
Tiny Tanganyikan cichlids that live in empty snail shells. Needs sand and shells, and hard, alkaline water.
Active, busy algae eater with a black stripe through the eye. Gets bigger than expected; keep in a small group.
Big, peaceful and plant-eating schooler. Needs a large tank, open water and hardy plants.
Active, silvery fish with white-tipped fins that may nip long fins. Keep six or more.
Active and hardy, eats pests but can bully smaller fish. Needs a lid.
Small, peaceful bottom feeder with a dark back stripe. Needs sand and a group of six or more.
Eats shrimp and small fish. Needs a lid and large tank.
Tiny gourami that makes clicks and grunts. Needs calm tank mates and floating plants.
Likes the top of the tank and jumps, so keep a tight lid. Peaceful in a group of six or more.
Compact, easy foreground or midground plant. Good for beginner scapes.
Warm-water cory with orange fins; a good match for discus tanks. Keep in groups.
Night-active, armored catfish with a talkative voice. May eat very small fish.
Thick-branched SPS that is a good first SPS. Needs strong light and good flow.
No photosynthesis, so must be target fed every day. Very hard to keep long-term.
Active, hardy livebearers with a sword on the male's tail. Males can chase each other; keep more females than males.
Small, shy blenny that grazes on rocks. Hardy and good for reefs.
Tall, double dorsal fins that spread like threads. Peaceful; keep in a calm tank.
Hardy and larger than most gouramis. Males can bully slower, smaller fish.
Hardy but aggressive as it grows. Best with other tough fish.
Bold fin-nippers. Only keep in a large group of eight or more and avoid long-finned fish such as bettas and angelfish.
Striped algae-eating snail. Needs hard water for a healthy shell and a lid.
Large and very active. Needs a huge tank and tank mates of similar size.
Bright red and bold. Gets aggressive as it ages; best alone or as a bonded pair.
Long sweeping tentacles that sting neighbors. Medium light, gentle flow; needs space.
Folded, fleshy coral that sits on sand. Low to medium light, gentle flow.
Algae eater that rights itself if flipped. A good reef clean-up crew.
Tanganyikan algae-grazer that lives in big groups. Needs hard, alkaline, clean water and a rocky tank.
Powerful algae eater, though it can knock over frags. Needs rock to graze on.
Blue-green and active, easy to keep. Likes neutral to hard water, a long tank and a group of six or more.
Strong algae grazer that can knock over frags. Needs a stable, mature tank.
Slow, twig-like catfish that eats algae and biofilm. Needs a mature, well-oxygenated tank and calm tank mates.
Odd catfish that swims belly-up and eats from the surface. Likes caves and groups.
Tall, ribbon-like leaves that spread fast by runners. Good background plant for most tanks.
Big filter feeder, calm and shy. Needs good flow and a mature tank.
Large, predatory Malawi peacock-type. Needs a large tank and hard, alkaline water.
Large floating plant with thick roots. Needs strong light; pond plant sometimes sold for tanks.
Large, floating rosettes with long roots. Needs good light and a gap between the leaves and the lid.
Fast, feathery plant that can be floated or planted. Great for soaking up nutrients.
Easy stem plant with broad lace-like leaves. Fast grower that fills the background.
Slim, flat bottom dweller with a whip-like tail. Peaceful and slow, needs sand and wood.
Cool-water, hardy and peaceful schooling fish. Good for unheated tanks and beginners.
Hardy, see-through tetra with a pale yellow glow. Does well in groups of six or more in a planted tank.
Pulsing coral that can grow fast and take over. Easy in some tanks, difficult in others.
Big wrasse that eats pests but also eats small inverts. Needs sand and a lid.
Bright yellow Malawi mbuna, active and territorial. Needs hard alkaline water and rock caves.
Bright golden neocaridina. Easy to keep in planted tanks with gentle tank mates.
Bright, active algae grazer that needs lots of swimming room. Does not mix well with other tangs of similar shape.
Sand-sifting goby that often pairs with a pistol shrimp. Needs sand and a lid.
Tough, boldly colored and territorial. Can harass peaceful tank mates.
Active loach with a pattern that looks like Y-O-Y-O. Needs a group and cover; may eat snails.
Bold, striped fish that is nearly bulletproof. Very active, so give it open water and a tight lid.
Small striped loach, active and social. May eat snails; keep a group.
Excellent algae eater. Will not breed in fresh water; needs hard water for its shell.
Rare, tiny black-and-white pleco that needs warm, very clean water and caves.
Colorful, easy coral that grows in colonies. Contains palytoxin, so handle with gloves.
